newsitem.title: UK: Funds concerned at MGAM over Horlick row.
newsitem.headline: Funds concerned at MGAM over Horlick row.

text.p: Pension funds invested with Morgan Grenfell Asset Management said on Monday they were concerned about MGAM's stability after a top fund manager quit last week but added they would not be spooked into a knee-jerk response.

The high-profile resignation of fund manager Nicola Horlick, whose team manages some 18 billion pounds ($30 billion) of UK pension fund money, came as a fresh blow to a firm still reeling from last year's sacking of fund manager Peter Young amid fund management irregularities.

"We have been concerned all the way since the Peter Young affair and this doesn't allay our fears at all," said David Tucker, treasury advisor for the London Borough of Lewisham which has 300 million pounds under sole management with MGAM.
"Obviously we are concerned," he said, adding the council was looking seriously at its pension management arrangements and was meeting next on March 4.
"A decision will be taken on that day as to whether to continue with the arrangements or offer (the management of the fund) for retendering," he said.

Horlick, dubbed "superwoman" by the British press, was suspended by MGAM last Tuesday for an alleged breach of contract just days after being promoted to managing director by chief executive Robert Smith.

A 35-year-old mother-of-five and one of the most prominent fund managers in London, she wants an amicable settlement with her ex-employer, her lawyer said on Monday, but is prepared to sue if they cannot strike a deal.
Alistair Barclay, finance manager for revenues at Dumfries and Galloway council in Scotland, was also worried but said the council would not be frightened into any hasty action.
"We are not going to be panicked into dumping Morgan Grenfell because of the actions of Nicola Horlick," he said.
"In terms of the fund's performance I have no complaints whatsoever," he said. "In terms of the stability of the fund I have some concerns."
He said Dumfries and Galloway, which has 200 million pounds invested with MGAM via its pension scheme, has a regular meeting scheduled for the end of February.
It is reviewing its options and will decide what, if any, action to take by May.
"We last reviewed Morgan Grenfell three years ago and their appointment is to be reviewed at the end of February," he said.
"We will consider a report on different options at that time...By May the members will decide which way they will go."
But Barclay stressed the council had a 20-year relationship with Morgan Grenfell and would not ditch that overnight in the wake of Horlick's acrimonious departure.
The Lewisham pension fund has 6,000 active contributers and 8,000 pensioners or deferred pensioners, and has been managed by MGAM for over two years. Before this it was managed in-house.
"We are taking a very serious view of it all and (the arrangement) is constantly under review," Tucker added.
An official at Westminister City Council which also has funds managed by MGAM said it too was keeping the situation with MGAM under review and had a meeting scheduled for February.
Both Dumfries and Galloway, and Lewisham councils have been impressed with MGAM's performance, particularly over the last three to four years, and are disappointed at recent events.

Barclay said what decision Dumfries and Galloway would take on the pension fund's management would be influenced by how well the MGAM team held together without Horlick, who had been considered an excellent staff manager.

But he said the council had taken heart from how well the morale of the team held up after the Peter Young affair. Young, who denies any criminal activity, is being investigated by Britain's serious Fraud Office after irregularities in funds he managed came to light.
"Nicola was head of a team but I don't imagine the rest of them will run out now," he said.
Clients on Monday received a statement from MGAM insisting that the investment team would hold together.
"Whatever you may have heard to the contrary, the members of the UK fund management team at Morgan Grenfell Investment Management remain entirely loyal to the business," it said.
"We wish to assure you in the strongest possible terms of the commitment of the team here to our clients and to the future success of Morgan Grenfell Investment Management."

But another MGAM client who declined to be named said that in an industry better known for its discretion he had doubts about the wisdom of some its staff decisions. "You have got to guess at some of their appointments," he said. ($1=.6021 Pound)
